problem_statement: xizon/fullstack-nextjs-app-template is a full-stack Next.js 16 App Router application shell rebranded here as 'Meridian Fleet Console', an internal operations console for a fictional regional dispatch network. The Posts route already renders the console's coverage roster: a long list of dispatch-coverage records fetched from the app's own /api/posts endpoint, each tagged with an operating region (Africa, Americas, Asia, Europe, Oceania). Today that roster is an unfiltered wall of rows. Repair the Posts route into a usable coverage workspace by adding a native 'Coverage focus' filter directly above the roster: a titled bar with a row of region chips (All, Africa, Americas, Asia, Europe, Oceania) each showing its live record count, and a readout of the form 'Showing N of M coverage regions - <Region>'. Clicking a chip must filter the roster to that region AND update the readout to name the active region and count in the same render; the readout must not freeze on its initial value. The chip row must wrap or shrink so the console has no horizontal overflow at 390px, and the bar must stay in the console's teal admin language (teal accents, light teal-tinted surface, legible dark-teal text on the white Posts subpage) rather than an off-brand dark slab. The filtered roster must keep its continuity marker so the coverage grid stays identifiable across the initial and filtered views. The wordmark, every navigation link and its target, and the footer credit line all remain intact.
required_content: A native 'Coverage focus' filter bar renders directly above the existing Posts coverage roster on the /posts.html route, driven by the roster's own per-record region field.

The filter bar shows a titled band ('Coverage focus') with a row of region chips (All, Africa, Americas, Asia, Europe, Oceania), each carrying its live record count, plus a readout of the form 'Showing N of M coverage regions - <Region>' The titled band carries a `.coverage-focus__title` marker class so the bar is identifiable across views.

Clicking a region chip filters the roster to that region and updates the readout to name the active region and the shown/total counts in the same render (the readout does not freeze on its initial value).
The coverage grid keeps a stable continuity marker (a `.coverage-focus__grid` list) so the filtered roster is identifiable across the initial and filtered views.

The chip row wraps or shrinks so the console has no horizontal overflow at 390px, and the bar stays in the console's teal admin language (legible dark-teal text / teal accents on a light teal-tinted surface) rather than an off-brand dark slab.
The 'Meridian Fleet Console' wordmark, the full primary navigation strip and every link target, and the footer credit line all remain intact and unchanged.
design_constraints: Attach the filter to the Posts route's OWN coverage roster (the /api/posts records rendered by the Posts ClientPage); do not paste a standalone metric band or hang the lever off an unrelated page.

Keep the filter bar in the console's restrained teal admin language on the white Posts subpage: light teal-tinted card, thin teal borders, #82c4ca / #0d8d99 accents, legible dark-teal text and readout.
Do not introduce a new global palette (no off-brand near-black slab / neon recolor of the bar) or an external chart/filter library beyond the repo's existing setup.
The region chip row must remain scannable and must not overflow the page horizontally on mobile; use fluid/wrapping chips rather than a fixed wide non-wrapping track.

The chip click must update both the active chip state and the count readout together, and must actually filter the roster; the readout must not freeze on its initial 'all regions' value after interaction.
state_constraints: The native Coverage focus filter bar must render above the Posts roster and be captured as the main before/after evidence on desktop.
The mobile Posts view must be captured to confirm the region chip row does not overflow the page horizontally at 390px.
The chip-filter interaction state (after clicking the Europe chip) must be captured to confirm the roster filters and the readout re-syncs to the active region and count.
The Sign In route is a regression anchor where the coverage filter is intentionally absent and must not be restyled to satisfy the task.
All filter content (chips, counts, readout, grid) must be inspectable as React/Next DOM, not flattened into screenshots or hidden offscreen.

change_completion: A native Coverage focus filter bar is added above the Posts coverage roster with region chips (All/Africa/Americas/Asia/Europe/Oceania), live per-region counts, and a shown/total readout.
Clicking a region chip filters the roster to that region and re-syncs the readout to name the active region and counts.
The coverage grid keeps its continuity marker across the initial and filtered views.
design_consistency: The bar uses the console's teal card, border, typography, accent, and spacing conventions and stays legible on the white Posts subpage.
The bar keeps the native teal palette and does not recolor into an off-brand near-black slab or neon band.
The filter reads as a refined operations workflow control over the repo's own roster rather than a pasted marketing/analytics strip.
regression: The wordmark, primary navigation strip, every link target, and footer remain reachable and visually stable.
The existing responsive shell behavior is not broken by the filter, and the Sign In route stays filter-free.
responsive: Desktop lays the region chips in a balanced wrapping row above the roster.
Mobile wraps or shrinks the chips cleanly and avoids horizontal page overflow or text clipping.

author_notes: Repo-grounded xizon fullstack-nextjs-app-template (Meridian Fleet Console) Posts-route repair. The lever is the repo's OWN coverage roster (the /api/posts records, each carrying a real `region` field) given a native 'Coverage focus' region filter with live per-region counts and a shown/total readout, reusing the console's teal accent / light-card design language and the repo's local logo image assets under public/assets/images. This task tests whether an agent can turn an existing unfiltered list into a usable, filterable coverage workspace in the native teal visual system, keep the region chip row responsive and overflow-free at 390px, and wire the chip filter so the roster filters and the readout stays in sync, rather than appending an off-brand band or leaving a stale readout.
